drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that one must praise God before making requests in prayer?
outcomeNote: The rule is grounded in Moses' own prayer; nothing is raised against it.

segments.he: דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי: לְעוֹלָם יְסַדֵּר אָדָם שִׁבְחוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִתְפַּלֵּל. מְנָלַן? — מִמֹּשֶׁה, דִּכְתִיב: ״וָאֶתְחַנַּן אֶל ה׳ בָּעֵת הַהִיא״. וּכְתִיב: ״ה׳ אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה הַחִלֹּתָ לְהַרְאוֹת אֶת עַבְדְּךָ אֶת גׇּדְלְךָ וְאֶת יָדְךָ הַחֲזָקָה אֲשֶׁר מִי אֵל בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה כְמַעֲשֶׂיךָ וְכִגְבוּרוֹתֶיךָ״. וּכְתִיב בָּתְרֵיהּ ״אֶעְבְּרָה נָּא וְאֶרְאֶה אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַטּוֹבָה וְגוֹ׳״.
segments.en: Based on Moses’ prayers, «Rabbi Simlai taught: One should always set forth praise of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and then pray» for his own needs. «From where do we» derive that one should conduct himself in this manner? «From Moses, as it is written» in his prayer: «“And I beseeched the Lord at that time”» (Deuteronomy 3:23). «And» immediately afterward in his prayer, «it is written: “Lord, God, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand, for what God is there in the heavens or on earth who can perform deeds such as Yours and Your might”» (Deuteronomy 3:24)? Here, Moses began with praise of God, «and it is» only «thereafter» that «it is written: “Please, let me pass over and see the good land» that is beyond the Jordan, that good hill country and the Lebanon” (Deuteronomy 3:25). Only after his praise did Moses make his personal request.
